āsaṅkā.p: [Ā+saki+a+ā] (thī) CL=8 (1) (a) wrong thinking . (B) worry. (2) a woman named Āsaṅkā.
pn: Āsaṅkā. The adopted daughter of the Bodhisatta in the Āsaṅkajātaka (Ja 380). She was so-called because she came to him when he crossed the water owing to his doubt (āsaṅkā) as to what was in the lotus. Ja.iii.250.
